title: Schroders seeks sale of Wisteria Mall in bid to offload Singapore properties
text:
Schroders seeks sale of Wisteria Mall in Singapore - The Business Times Search
 Subscribe Schroders seeks sale of Wisteria Mall in bid to offload Singapore properties
 It has appointed Knight Frank and Savills to raise around S$220 million from the sale

 The mall was bought in 2022 for S$208 million by Schroders’ Pamfleet Real Estate Fund III, according to a media report at the time. PHOTO: CMG 
 [SINGAPORE] Schroders is planning to sell off some of its real estate assets in Singapore, having appointed a pair of brokers to raise around S$220 million from the sale of a mall, according to people familiar with the matter.
 The London-based asset manager, which was acquired by Nuveen last month, wants to sell Wisteria Mall, a suburban two-storey retail asset in northern Singapore, according to people familiar with the matter.
 Brokers Knight Frank and Savills are running an expression of interest exercise that is due to close in late November, the people said, asking for anonymity to speak about a private process.
 The mall was bought in 2022 for S$208 million by Schroders’ Pamfleet Real Estate Fund III, according to a media report at the time. It has an occupancy level of 93 per cent, according to the people.
 The attempted sale will add to an earlier push to sell off a hotel in the city-state that Schroders co-owns with TPG Angelo Gordon. A sale process was conducted by Jones Lang LaSalle for S$320 million in 2024, although the asset has yet to be sold.
 “We regularly review our real estate portfolios and consider opportunities in the best interests of our investors,” said a spokesperson for Schroders Capital, the firm’s private markets investment arm. A Savills spokesperson declined to comment. A Knight Frank spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
